re_line: China iron ore pricing fight escalates · Albanese signs Philippines defence pact at ASEAN · Solomon Islands alleges 'chequebook diplomacy' · Wong blasts Israel over Gaza aid · Roy Morgan has Coalition ahead for first time since 2025
morning_memo: Canberra hardened its line on China's centralised iron ore buying, warning the scheme may breach trade rules as Goldman Sachs estimates Beijing will save $14.8 billion over a decade.
Solomon Islands opposition MPs accused Australia of chequebook diplomacy over grants they say flow to government MPs.
New Zealand officials head to Washington for a December 1 US International Trade Commission remedies hearing on lamb imports already carrying a 13.2 percent tariff.

top_stories.headline: Albanese signs Philippines defence pact as ASEAN summit opens in Manila
top_stories.body: **Anthony Albanese** signed the Philippines-Australia Defense Cooperation Arrangement in Manila ahead of the 49th ASEAN summit, with South China Sea tensions topping the agenda when he met his Philippine counterpart. The Diplomat notes the agreement builds on earlier bilateral accords including the 2007 Status of Visiting Forces Agreement. **Donald Trump** is due for the summit's final day, and a Quad leaders meeting bringing together Australia, India, Japan and the United States is expected on the margins before leaders travel to China for APEC.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News: "What's at stake at the 49th ASEAN summit?" · also The Diplomat

top_stories.headline: Canberra hardens stance on China's centralised iron ore buying
top_stories.body: Australia sharpened its warning that China's centralised iron ore purchasing could breach trade rules, Bloomberg reports, a step up from its earlier caution over the weekend. **Madeleine King** may intervene, according to the Australian Financial Review, after Goldman Sachs estimated China will save close to *$14.8 billion* on iron ore purchases over the next decade through buying coordinated by CMRG. Australian producers have put the potential revenue damage at $10 billion.
top_stories.src_line: per Bloomberg: "Australia Hardens Its Stance on China's Iron-Ore Pricing Efforts" · also AFR

top_stories.headline: Wong joins allied ministers condemning Israel over blocked Gaza aid
top_stories.body: **Penny Wong** said it was unacceptable that Israel is preventing *150,000 tents* and other vital supplies from entering Gaza, in a joint statement with the United Kingdom, Italy and France. The United Nations says more than 40,000 tents housing displaced Palestinians have been damaged by rain and flooding. The signatories said vital supplies are sitting at the border and must be let in immediately.
top_stories.src_line: per SMH Federal Politics (Matthew Knott): "'Stop the delays': Wong, counterparts blast Israel over Gaza humanitarian crisis" · also ABC News

top_stories.headline: Australia joins seven-nation US-led Pax Silica pact on AI supply chains
top_stories.body: Australia is one of seven founding members of Pax Silica, a United States-led arrangement to protect artificial intelligence supply chains from China, the Australian Financial Review reports. The grouping was formed amid concern over Beijing's progress in AI and its hold on rare earth supplies. It adds a technology and critical minerals layer to Washington's efforts to coordinate allied industrial policy responses.
top_stories.src_line: per AFR: "Australia joins US pact to protect AI supply chains from China"

overnight_items.headline: Albanese pressed from across the spectrum to skip Putin photo at APEC
overnight_items.body_text: **Anthony Albanese** faces calls from across the political spectrum and from the Ukrainian diaspora to refuse a group photograph with **Vladimir Putin** at the APEC summit in China, the Sydney Morning Herald reports. The Australian Financial Review reports critics argue any joint appearance would risk normalising Putin on the world stage and undermine Australia's support for Ukraine. Albanese has not ruled the photograph out.

overnight_items.headline: Energy shocks, AI and Myanmar dominate the ASEAN agenda in Manila
overnight_items.body_text: Middle East conflict and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz have pushed energy security to the top of the ASEAN agenda, with South-East Asia heavily dependent on Gulf oil and gas. **Hunter Marston**, South-East Asia program director at the Lowy Institute, told the ABC the issue had been "massive" and had triggered protests. ASEAN is pressing progress on a strategic petroleum reserve and a regional power grid.

overnight_items.headline: Megaspeed says alleged Chinese agent left firm in 2025 as chip probe widens
overnight_items.body_text: Singapore-based Megaspeed International says Chinese citizen **Alice Huang** left the company effective August 30, 2025, and has retained outside counsel for an internal investigation. The firm is under United States scrutiny over reported shipments of advanced Nvidia AI chips to China in breach of export restrictions. Huang's relationship with former Nvidia chief executive **Jensen Huang** has triggered American national security concerns and multiple congressional investigations.

overnight_items.headline: Ken Wyatt named Western Australia's first Indigenous governor
overnight_items.body_text: **Ken Wyatt**, the first Indigenous Australian elected to the House of Representatives, has been named Western Australia's next governor, the ABC reports. The appointment makes him the first Indigenous person to hold the office in the state that hosts the bulk of Australia's resources exports and its submarine infrastructure at Henderson and HMAS Stirling.

overnight_items.headline: European states look to Rwanda deportations modelled on Australia's offshore scheme
overnight_items.body_text: Denmark and other European countries want to deport asylum seekers to Rwanda, in what the Sydney Morning Herald describes as an echo of Australia's Pacific solution. Australian offshore processing continues to be cited as a template by European governments facing migration pressure, two decades after it was first adopted.

overnight_items.headline: Anti-dumping investigation opened into Chinese timber imports
overnight_items.body_text: Australia has opened an investigation into alleged dumping of Chinese timber, The Australian reports, with cheap imports said to threaten domestic housing supply chains and jobs. The inquiry lands the same day Canberra escalated its complaint over Chinese iron ore buying practices.

aukus_watch.headline: Lowy piece says AUKUS Public Inquiry doubts Washington but not Beijing
aukus_watch.body_text: The Lowy Interpreter argues the AUKUS Public Inquiry questions Washington's motives at length while barely scrutinising Beijing's. The inquiry has been a recurring venue for Australian criticism of the submarine pact's reliance on United States delivery schedules.

pacific_wire.headline: Solomon Islands opposition accuses Australia of 'chequebook diplomacy'
pacific_wire.body_text: Solomon Islands opposition politicians have accused Australia of chequebook diplomacy over grants they say are directed to government MPs, the ABC reports. Solomon Islands Prime Minister **Jeremiah Manele** currently chairs the Pacific Islands Forum.

pacific_wire.headline: Tuvalu rejects relocation: 'We are not planning to abandon our homeland'
pacific_wire.body_text: Tuvalu told the COP31 talks it will not abandon its territory to sea level rise. "We are not planning to abandon our homeland. We are planning to protect our people, our identity and our future," Islands Business quotes. Tuvalu also warned that rising seas threaten its sovereignty and called for urgent climate action and energy investment.

pacific_wire.headline: Tonga declares drought across most islands as El Nino persists
pacific_wire.body_text: Tonga has declared drought across most of its islands, with El Nino effects expected to persist until at least June next year, Islands Business reports. The prime minister used the declaration to press for stronger global climate action at COP31.

pacific_wire.headline: Green Climate Fund directs $3.5 billion to 14 Pacific states, eyes Suva office
pacific_wire.body_text: The Green Climate Fund has directed $3.5 billion to 14 Pacific Island countries and is moving to establish a regional office in Fiji, according to PACNEWS. Pacific negotiators at COP31 also pressed for the High Seas Treaty to protect migratory ocean corridors.

pacific_wire.headline: Cook Islands met service warns of strong El Nino and active cyclone season
pacific_wire.body_text: The Cook Islands meteorological service has urged communities to prepare for an active cyclone season and continued El Nino conditions despite recent rain. The warning follows regional forecasts that the El Nino event will disrupt weather into early 2027.

pacific_wire.headline: Vanuatu solar scheme aimed at reducing violence wins international recognition
pacific_wire.body_text: A ni-Vanuatu woman has been recognised internationally for a solar lighting scheme designed to reduce male violence against women, the ABC reports. The programme links energy access to community safety outcomes in a country where gender-based violence rates are among the region's highest.

pacific_wire.headline: PNG seeks Australian treatment for conjoined twins born in East New Britain
pacific_wire.body_text: Conjoined twin girls delivered two weeks ago at Nonga Base Hospital in East New Britain are being flown to Port Moresby, with enquiries under way about transfer to Australia because Papua New Guinea's health system cannot treat them. It is PNG's second conjoined twin case in just over a year. **Jurgen Ruh**, who founded an NGO providing emergency obstetric care in PNG, said he was approaching four countries for help and that Australia was "our favourite".

pacific_wire.headline: Kiribati mourns a death as Pacific leaders press COP31 for action over talk
pacific_wire.body_text: PACNEWS reports Kiribati is in mourning and that Pacific political champions at COP31 called for less talk and more action. The United Nations climate chief urged delegations in Antalya to accelerate negotiations and convert commitments into delivery.

pacific_wire.headline: New Zealand charity takes up case of woman stranded three years in Cook Islands
pacific_wire.body_text: Deen Welfare Trust has engaged immigration lawyers for **Ruchira Rajasingha**, a 50-year-old Sri Lankan woman stuck in the Cook Islands since November 2023 because New Zealand and Australia have repeatedly refused transit visas. Cook Islands Immigration has been unable to deport her. Trust representative **Tahir Nawaz** said the priority was getting her safely home.

new_zealand.headline: New Zealand sends officials to Washington over US lamb safeguard probe
new_zealand.body_text: New Zealand officials will argue at the US International Trade Commission's remedies hearing on December 1, after the panel decided to investigate whether lamb imports harm American farmers. New Zealand beef and lamb exports to the United States run at *$660 million* a year and already face a 13.2 percent tariff. Beef and Lamb chair **Kate Acland** said commissioners were evenly split on whether New Zealand product was hurting local producers, with **Donald Trump** expected to make the final call early next year.

new_zealand.headline: Final New Zealand election results due November 27, three weeks after polling day
new_zealand.body_text: The Electoral Commission will publish final results on Friday November 27, the same three-week interval as 2023 despite changes to early enrolment rules, **Christopher Luxon** was told on Morning Report. Luxon also faces questions over the National Party's direction after outgoing MP **Vanessa Weenink** said the party had gone too far to the right.

china_in_the_pacific.headline: Retired Marine colonel warns United States is losing a contest it has not recognised
china_in_the_pacific.body_text: Retired Marine colonel **Grant Newsham** argues the future of the Pacific Islands may prove critical not only to regional security but to the strategic balance of the entire Indo-Pacific, the Pacific Island Times reports. The piece frames Chinese influence building in the islands as a competition Washington is already behind in.

canberra_politics.headline: Roy Morgan has Coalition leading on two-party and primary vote for first time since 2025
canberra_politics.body_text: Roy Morgan's federal voting intention survey puts the Liberal-National Coalition ahead of Labor on both two-party preferred and primary vote for the first time since the 2025 federal election. **Angus Taylor** has led the Liberals since February 2026. The next federal election must be held on or before 20 May 2028.

canberra_politics.headline: Greens complicate Chalmers' capital gains package before the Senate rises
canberra_politics.body_text: **Jim Chalmers** wants his capital gains tax changes through the Senate this year, but the Greens say a separate plan from independent **Allegra Spender** is worth examining. The Australian reports Labor's accompanying $43 billion trust measures hinge on a single Greens demand.

canberra_politics.headline: Husic becomes first Labor MP to call for independent control of staffing allocations
canberra_politics.body_text: Former minister **Ed Husic** says the number of staff allocated to each MP should be set independently rather than by the prime minister, the first Labor MP to break cover on the question. Staffing allocation has been a long-running grievance among backbenchers and the crossbench.

canberra_politics.headline: Gas producers warn of 'dire consequences' as Coalition seeks WA carve-out
canberra_politics.body_text: Gas producers say Labor's reservation plan, which would keep 20 percent of exports onshore, risks national energy security. The Coalition wants Western Australia carved out of the scheme and the Greens want the measure pushed further, leaving the government squeezed from both sides as the parliamentary year ends.

canberra_politics.headline: Independent MP Helen Haines discharged from hospital after alleged vehicle attack
canberra_politics.body_text: Independent member **Helen Haines** has left hospital after an alleged attack involving an SUV, The Australian and the Washington Post report. Haines holds Indi as one of ten independents in the 150-seat House of Representatives.

canberra_politics.headline: Victorian leaders pressed for a full audit of state finances before the election
canberra_politics.body_text: **Ben Carroll** and **Jess Wilson** face calls to publish a complete account of Victoria's finances ahead of the state election, The Australian reports. Victorian debt has become a recurring theme in a campaign the federal parties are watching for signals on tax and spending.

business_economy.headline: PIMCO warns of a sustained diesel crunch for Australia
business_economy.body_text: **Greg Sharenow**, head of commodities at PIMCO, told the Australian Financial Review that a lesson from this year's United States-Iran crisis should be an "all energy" approach to meeting rising demand, and that Australia faces a sustained diesel squeeze. Brent crude traded at 95.30, up 2.74 percent.

business_economy.headline: Coles discloses cyber incident to the ASX with little detail
business_economy.body_text: Coles told the stock exchange it is investigating a cybersecurity incident and has found no evidence that customer, team or supplier data was taken. The supermarket group is working with global cybersecurity experts and is examining problems affecting a small number of Liquorland click-and-collect customers. The ASX 200 closed at 9,045, up 0.17 percent.

primary_documents.headline: Joint Foreign Ministers Statement on Gaza
primary_documents.body_text: Wong's office published the joint foreign ministers statement on Gaza co-signed with counterparts from the United Kingdom, Italy and France, demanding Israel permit the immediate entry of blocked humanitarian supplies.

calendar_watch.event: Final day of the 49th ASEAN summit in Manila, with Trump attending and a Quad leaders meeting expected on the margins
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Albanese's bilateral program and any Quad statement set the tone before leaders move to APEC in China.

calendar_watch.event: Scheduled close of COP31 in Antalya
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Pacific delegations are pressing for text on fossil fuels and finance after Tuvalu and Tonga raised sovereignty and drought at the talks.

calendar_watch.event: New Zealand Electoral Commission publishes final 2026 election results
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Final counts and special votes determine whether Luxon can form a government and on what coalition terms.

calendar_watch.event: US International Trade Commission remedies hearing on lamb imports
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: New Zealand's $660 million beef and lamb trade to the United States, already tariffed at 13.2 percent, is exposed to further measures.

calendar_watch.event: Salvage window for the Indonesian barge Nelly 112 aground in the Torres Strait
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: The 3.7-metre tides needed to refloat the wreck occur only in cyclone season, keeping an unresolved foreign wreck on Australian territory.

key_stat.label: China's projected iron ore savings over a decade
key_stat.context: Goldman Sachs estimates centralised buying by CMRG will cut China's iron ore bill by that amount, the figure behind Canberra's hardened trade-rules warning.

also_today.headline: Fiji should operate its Bluebottles jointly with Australia
also_today.body_text: The ASPI Strategist argues Fiji should run its Bluebottle uncrewed surveillance boats jointly with Australia rather than alone, and that the capability Fiji actually needs independently is tasking, deciding where and when the boats go.

also_today.headline: Just by meeting, Quad leaders send a signal to Beijing
also_today.body_text: China's longstanding opposition to the Quad heightens the political significance of this week's leaders meeting in Manila, ASPI argues, with the gathering of Australia, India, Japan and the United States carrying weight regardless of its deliverables.

also_today.headline: Why resource benefit sharing keeps missing the poorest women
also_today.body_text: **AW Syaiful Huda**, director of the Bojonegoro Institute, writes that Indonesia's Bojonegoro district sits on one of the country's richest oil fields yet retains high poverty, with women trailing men in income and schooling. The post draws on a 2025 assessment and social registry analysis by the institute.

also_today.headline: Nearly half of federal parliament has taken foreign or private-funded travel since 2019
also_today.body_text: Crikey's review of parliamentary disclosures finds nearly half of federal parliamentarians have accepted overseas travel funded by foreign governments, think tanks or private interests since 2019, with little scrutiny of whose interests are served.

also_today.headline: Indonesian barge still aground in Torres Strait ten months on
also_today.body_text: The 100-metre Indonesian barge Nelly 112 remains grounded on Athikho Poji near Badu Island after drifting across international waters in January. Salvage specialist **Vance Wallin** has a plan but is waiting on the owner's overseas insurers and the 3.7-metre tides that occur only between December and March.

opeds_today.headline: First Nations IP protection risks going from "miracle to mirage"
opeds_today.central_argument: A new international treaty strengthens Australia's case for domestic reform on Indigenous intellectual property, but only if major economies also sign.
opeds_today.summary: The piece argues the treaty's value depends on broad ratification, and that without the large economies joining, protection for First Nations knowledge remains nominal. Australia's domestic reform case is strengthened by the instrument regardless.
opeds_today.policy_so_what: Shapes Australian positioning in WIPO negotiations and the domestic legislative agenda on Indigenous cultural and intellectual property.

opeds_today.headline: Philippines, Australia Sign New Defense Agreement Amid China Pressure
opeds_today.central_argument: The new Defense Cooperation Agreement extends a layered set of bilateral accords between Canberra and Manila under Chinese maritime pressure.
opeds_today.summary: The Diplomat notes the agreement builds on prior instruments including the 2007 Status of Visiting Forces Agreement. It places the signing in the context of sustained Chinese activity in the South China Sea.
opeds_today.policy_so_what: Defines the legal scaffolding for expanded Australian Defence Force activity in and around the Philippines.
